subject: 🏃 Tuesday — 3×1600m Track Sharpener (Wk 7, Presidio Pivot Week)
html:
Tomorrow: 3×1600m threshold on the high-school track. This is a taper sharpener for Sunday's Presidio HM pivot test — keep the snap, skip the volume. Warm up with the 1.9-mi jog to the track, run the 3 reps at 7:15–7:25/mi (threshold pace-anchored — 1600m is long enough for HR to settle, but pace is the primary target here), 2 min recovery jog between reps, then 1.9 mi jog home. ~7–8 mi total.

Pre-run activation: quadruped hip CARs (3 each direction, each leg), banded lateral walks (10 each), glute bridges (10 reps), quadruped banded hip IR (5–10 each side, PT-prescribed). On the track, add 2–3 strides after the warm-up jog before Rep 1 to open the legs up.

The reps are trimmed from 5×1600m to 3×1600m — this was an intentional edit after Saturday's 14.23-mi long run (suffer 231, 82% Z3) and the June 9 cumulative-fatigue flag. You don't need more fitness this week; you need to arrive Sunday fresh with your legs remembering what threshold pace feels like. If the legs feel genuinely flat or heavy on Rep 1, drop to 2 reps and jog home. If they feel great, cap at 3 — do not add reps back. The Presidio HM is the workout that matters this week.

Focus cue: Smooth turnover and relaxed shoulders through each rep. You ran 7:01–7:23 for the first two threshold miles in Boston on jet-lag day 2 — fresh legs on your home track should feel easy at 7:15–7:25. If pace is coming out faster than 7:15 and the effort feels controlled, that's fine — just don't chase it. Let the snap come to you.

Where you are: Week 7 of 12, Phase 2. 5 days to the Presidio Half Marathon pivot test (June 21). Knee has been 1/5 for every V6 session except one (Boston stairs). Monday's hip circuit was clean. The three gates Sunday: sub-1:37:30 finish, avg HR <170 final 3 mi, zero knee compensation. Tomorrow sharpens the legs; Wed–Sat protects them. Lay out your track gear tonight, set the alarm, and get to bed by 10 — this one should feel crisp and short.
